items.title: Steve "Ted" Brown Interview, 1958-04-22
items.q: But a great many times I'd play with Jack Lane and his band. He'd want me to play tuba for him.

ctx.x: We'll look it up. We'll find it. It might take a while but we'll do it.

Well yes. Well in a way. That was our first brass band job. Then we had became acquainted with Jack Lane. Jack Lane more or less had brass bands. He didn't fool around with orchestra much. He had a big brass band. He was a bass drummer himself. And whenever he had orchestra jobs, he'd give us a lot of orchestra jobs. But a great many times I'd play with Jack Lane and his band. He'd want me to play tuba for him. And Tom would be hired in different positions. We all worked along with different others. But we got so…
Did he write left-handed and eat left-handed? Or just played the trumpet that way?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: I had Tom and Teddoh playing with me.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you, did Tom Brown play with you? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. He's one of the two Teddors. I had Tom and Teddoh playing with me. Yeah. I had five bands Johnny going all the time. Steve Brown played with you too, huh? That's Ted. That's his name. Who? Ted, huh? Ted. Ted. They called him Steve later on. Yeah. Teddoh. Yeah. Teddoh. Uh-huh. Yeah. They called him Steve. Yeah. He was in town recently too. Yeah, I know. I met him. He looked me up. Yeah. He's a wonderful bass player.
There's Merritt. He's good bass player. He's right here. Merritt.
